opportunities.name: Tech project lead research (HN + GitHub → note)
opportunities.description: For a given open-source project, find its top Hacker News story, open its GitHub repo to read stars and latest release, then log a 'Lead:' note summarizing both.
steps: Open the Hacker News search (Algolia), clear the query box and type {project}, then press Enter
Read the top story's title, points and age
On GitHub, open 'Search or jump to', type {project} and press Enter
Click the top repository result (e.g. owner/{project})
Read the star count and the latest release date
Open the Notes app, click 'New note'
Type 'Lead: {project}. HN "{top story title}" ({points} pts, {age}); GitHub {stars} stars, last release {release date}' and press Enter

instances.values: project=Bun (HN 2192 pts, GitHub 96.2k stars); interrupted by CourtListener searches

opportunities.name: Company legal-story pitch (CourtListener + Wikipedia → email)
opportunities.description: For a given company, search CourtListener for case law, open a notable case, look up the company on Wikipedia for HQ and CEO, then draft a pitch email to an editor.
steps: On CourtListener, click the 'Keyword(s) search' box, select all and type {company}, then press Enter
Open a relevant opinion from the results and note the case name, court and filing date
On Wikipedia, search for {company} and open the company article (pick the 'Inc.' entry from the disambiguation page if one appears)
Read the headquarters and CEO
In Mail, compose a new message to {recipient}
Set Subject to 'Pitch: {company} in court'
Set Body to 'Hi {name}, {case} ({court}, filed {date}). {company}: HQ {hq}, CEO {ceo}. Worth a piece?' and send (or discard)

instances.values: company=Uber, case=Uber v. Uber (Ohio Ct. App. 2017), recipient=lena@example.com; draft was discarded
company=Airbnb; CourtListener search only, did not continue
company=Tesla; CourtListener search, then Wikipedia 'Tesla, Inc.'; no email written

opportunities.name: Country fact-check (World Bank data + BBC news → note)
opportunities.description: For a given country, get a key development indicator (life expectancy) from World Bank Open Data, find a recent related BBC News story, and log a 'Fact-check' note.
steps: On World Bank Open Data, click the 'Search data' box, type {country}, and pick the country from the suggestions (use the World Bank spelling, e.g. 'Viet Nam')
Read life expectancy at birth and its year on the country page
On BBC, open the menu, type '{country} {topic}' in 'Search news, topics and more' and press Enter
Open the top relevant article and note its headline and age
Open the Notes app, click 'New note'
Type 'Fact-check {country}: Life expectancy at birth {value} ({year}). Context: {headline} ({age})' and press Enter

instances.values: country=Kenya, topic=health; life expectancy 64 (2024); Ebola article; note saved
country=Vietnam / Viet Nam, topic=climate; Kenya vs Viet Nam comparison (75); coffee article opened; no note
country=Argentina; World Bank search tried several times, never got past the search box
